subject: kraken
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: kraken rising, tentacles spread.
Style: Overwatch.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out the kraken design in an Overwatch-inspired style: a tilted mantle head, two eyes, a beak, and eight radiating tentacles with suckers, rising dramatically from the water with clean, bright stylized colors.

For the skeleton, I'm setting up a core joint, mantle joint, and tentacle chains rooted at the body, curving outward with tips resting on the ground. Each tentacle gets swept geometry with gradient coloring (purple top, pink underside) and sucker details placed along the underside using embedded stick parts, repeated across all eight limbs.

Now I'm placing the body parts -- a mantle cone tilted back, head sphere, and eyes made from glowing spheres with a dark slit pupil facing forward. For the tentacle positions, I'm working out a curved path for each limb with varying height and outward reach so some rise up dramatically while others drape toward the ground, giving the kraken an asymmetric, dynamic pose.

I'm distributing eight tentacles around the +Z front using angled directions off a base ring, naming them simply by index. Two of the rear tentacles get a distinct raised path, arcing upward high instead of resting on the floor, while the others taper normally toward the ground.

Now I'm shaping the mantle as a tall tilted cone-like sphere scaled and rotated backward, placing the head sphere forward near it, and adding spikes along the mantle using the two-point spike helper with the length set to null so it's derived from the point pair.

For the beak, I'm setting up a jaw joint attached to the head, then building upper and lower beak cones as spikes positioned near the jaw pivot, considering whether to use the sweep helper instead for more control over tapering, and finally posing the jaw open slightly like the earlier examples.

I'm also laying out the main joint hierarchy—core, mantle, and head joints—then thinking through coloring the body: countershading the mantle between purple-blue spotted top and pink belly, and giving the tentacles a procedural paint where the upper surface is purple and the underside shifts to coral based on angle.

Now I'm adding glowing cyan orbs studded along the mantle for bioluminescence, and placing the eyes as small spheres with yellow glowing sclera and slit pupils, checking that their position sits just inside the head sphere's surface near the front.

I'm positioning the pupils as thin ellipsoids tucked into the eye spheres, and adding heavy angled brow shapes rotated to give an aggressive Overwatch-villain expression. I'm deciding to skip a full water base and just keep things minimal, maybe adding a small foam ring later if needed.

Now I'm scripting sucker placement along the tentacle sweep, stepping through parameter values to stick small pink cylinders at each point with radius scaling along the tentacle length, aiming for roughly eighty suckers total. Next I'm planning spike crests along the mantle's back by positioning spike shapes manually along the mantle's central axis.

Still computing spike placement vectors... For the fins, I'll just use flattened, rotated spheres on the mantle sides instead of extruded outlines to keep it simple, and cap the tentacle tips with rounded spheres.

Writing tentacle sweep code with mottled purple-to-pink coloring, giving tips a magenta glow and using countershading-style mottling across the mantle and head for texture.
